grades.quote: If software modifies a leaf PTE, it should execute SFENCE.VMA with rs1 set to a virtual address within the page. If any PTE along the traversal path had its G bit set, rs2 must be_ `x0` _; otherwise, rs2 should be set to the ASID for which the translation is being modified.
grades.reason: Explains when SFENCE.VMA is needed after page-table or satp changes, and how rs1/rs2 select the scope (leaf vs non-leaf PTE, ASID, global mappings). It doesn't state the ordering and invalidation semantics directly.

grades.quote: an SFENCE.VMA instruction with rs1=_ `x0` _will therefore either terminate all previously-launched speculative executions of the addresstranslation algorithm (for the specified ASID, if applicable), or simply wait for them to complete (in which case any address-translation cache entries created will be invalidated by the SFENCE.VMA as appropriate)
grades.reason: Describes how SFENCE.VMA interacts with speculative page-table walks and address-translation cache entries. It either terminates the walks or waits for them to complete, so stale PTEs are not cached. This is useful but only covers part of the synchronization.

grades.quote: The SFENCE.VMA instruction must be used to_  _ensure that updates to the address-translation data structures are observed by subsequent implicit reads to those structures by a hart.
grades.reason: The passage states that SFENCE.VMA ensures page-table (address-translation data structure) updates are observed by subsequent implicit reads by a hart. It also says that writing satp implies no ordering or cache invalidation, so SFENCE.VMA may be needed after a page-table modification or ASID reuse. This answers the query directly, though it appears in the satp section and not in the SFENCE.VMA section.

grades.quote: If _rs1_ = `x0` and _rs2_ ≠ `x0` , the fence orders all reads and writes made to any level of the page tables, but only for the address space identified by integer register _rs2_ . Accesses to _global_ mappings (see Section 12.3.1) are not ordered. The fence also invalidates all address-translation cache entries matching the address space identified by integer register _rs2_ , except for entries containing global mappings.
grades.reason: Directly states the ordering and invalidation guarantees of SFENCE.VMA. It orders reads and writes to page-table entries, scoped by the rs1/rs2 operands, and invalidates matching address-translation cache entries.
